method: Actual CUA browser interaction and read-only rendered DOM inspection; no fetch mocks, hidden React state access or injected game fixtures.

observations.detail: Started a real local game; HUD score=0, lines=0, level=1, gravity=500 ms; Hold EMPTY and enabled. DOM contained exactly 200 board cells, 20 row indices and 10 column indices.
Clicked Hold (C Key): EMPTY disappeared, a canonical occupied Hold preview appeared, and button became disabled until lock. Screenshot records the occupied slot and disabled button.
Restarted to a fresh session with EMPTY Hold; pressed lowercase c; Hold became occupied and disabled.
Restarted independently to EMPTY Hold; pressed shift+c (uppercase C); Hold became occupied and disabled.

Restarted with O at columns 4/5; Left moved its visible columns to 3/4; Right returned them to 4/5. Gravity continued during observation. Down was accepted during play with zero HUD score; exact soft-drop behavior is additionally covered by generated tests, not inferred from wall-clock row changes.
Allowed normal gravity to fill the board: GAME_OVER appeared with modal, Hold disabled, Play Again and Restart Game controls. No board or API state was injected.
Clicked the modal Restart Game: new session ID 9c7b220e..., PLAYING, score/lines=0, level=1, 500 ms, EMPTY Hold and enabled button.

captures.caption: Actual local UI: initial counters, board, next preview and empty Hold. Gravity continued while capturing.
Actual local UI: occupied Hold, next preview, board and disabled Hold control before the next lock.
Actual local UI: natural blocked-spawn game over and restart modal.

limitations: Manual browser play did not reach level 2 or the 100 ms floor. Exact timer boundaries and asynchronous request ownership require the fake-clock/deferred-request suite.
Three- and four-row scoring are isolated-domain fixtures, not manually reached browser clears.
Separate derived quality/usage panels must be labeled as derived views of retained raw outputs, never native Sonar UI or terminal screenshots.
